title: This week's hottest mathematics papers on arXiv

sections.title: The isoperimetric inequality and CMC hypersurfaces in Cartan-Hadamard manifolds
sections.abstract: The authors claim the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality for domains in complete simply connected nonpositively curved manifolds in dimensions 3 through 9, establishing the Cartan–Hadamard conjecture in that range.
sections.claimed_result: The paper says it proves the sharp Euclidean isoperimetric inequality using a sharp inequality for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces, Jacobi-field estimates, and an isoperimetric-profile argument.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete, connected, simply connected Riemannian manifolds with nonpositive sectional curvature in dimensions 3–9; singular isoperimetric boundaries may occur.
sections.caveat: An arXiv preprint claim requiring expert verification; the ranking reflects significance if correct, not independent proof validation.

sections.title: Boolean Small-Ball Inequalities for Discrepancy Theory
sections.abstract: The authors prove small-ball inequalities for random-sign matrix series and derive an interlacing-free route to Kadison–Singer together with consequences for Matrix Spencer, Komlós, and other discrepancy problems.
sections.claimed_result: For Boolean matrix series under stated variance bounds, the paper proves a determinant small-ball lower bound and says this yields an interlacing-free proof of general Kadison–Singer plus discrepancy corollaries.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Symmetric matrix coefficients with uniformly random signs; coefficient energy and an additional variance term must satisfy universal bounds.
sections.caveat: The exact hypotheses and each claimed consequence should be checked in the full 37-page preprint.

sections.title: Universal completeness of exponentials
sections.abstract: The authors construct uniformly discrete frequency sets whose exponential systems are complete in every finite-p space over every measurable set below a prescribed measure threshold, and establish sharpness results for related uniqueness conditions.
sections.claimed_result: The paper constructs density-one universal frequency sets, density-v integer-frequency constructions, a negative result for asymptotically integer sets, and a sharp Sobolev threshold; Lean code is linked from the record.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Exponential systems on measurable subsets of the real line with uniformly discrete frequency sets and stated density and measure constraints; higher-dimensional extensions are claimed.
sections.caveat: The scope of the linked formalization and the full mathematical proof remain to be checked separately.

sections.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions to the 3D Navier–Stokes equations with analytic forcing
sections.abstract: Under specific anisotropic Type-II bounds and an exactly axisymmetric collapsing core, the authors claim that analytic forcing prevents a putative finite-time singularity in 3D Navier–Stokes.
sections.claimed_result: The paper says such solutions are regular at the proposed singular point and derives constraints on any force used in a construction of that type.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: 3D Navier–Stokes with real-analytic body force, stated anisotropic bounds, and exact axisymmetry in a collapsing core; the proof uses blow-up limits and rigidity.
sections.caveat: This excludes a specified mechanism, not general 3D blow-up; the abstract also references another manuscript whose status should be verified.

sections.title: Generic Uniqueness of Isoperimetric Regions in Arbitrary Dimension
sections.abstract: For a generic smooth Riemannian metric on a closed connected manifold, the authors claim uniqueness of the isoperimetric region at every prescribed non-half volume, with exactly a complementary pair at half volume.
sections.claimed_result: For each non-half volume fraction, a generic metric has a unique isoperimetric region; at half volume it has exactly two complementary minimizers.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Closed connected smooth manifolds, smooth Riemannian metrics, and prescribed volume fractions; the proof does not require boundary regularity or Jacobi nondegeneracy.
sections.caveat: Genericity is a Baire-category statement, not a claim for every metric; singular-boundary arguments require specialist review.

sections.title: On the ACC for Minimal Log Discrepancies for Bounded Generalized Sub-Pairs
sections.abstract: The authors claim the ascending chain condition for minimal log discrepancies for bounded generalized sub-pairs in arbitrary dimension and for bounded threefolds with arbitrary boundaries.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract states the ACC conjecture for minimal log discrepancies holds in the two stated bounded settings.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Bounded generalized sub-pairs in arbitrary dimension, or bounded threefolds with arbitrary boundaries; precise boundedness definitions are essential.
sections.caveat: The abstract gives little proof strategy or detail about the boundary of the hypotheses, so the exact scope requires reading the paper.
